n181b6c9daaa.s: Which of the following is NOT a Section 24 exempt organisation under the RTI Act, 2005, being the appellate information body?
n181b6c9daaa.x: The Central Information Commission is the appellate information body and is not a Section 24 exempt organisation. The IB, R&AW and CRPF are covered by Section 24.

nca6b0ff6c16.s: Which of the following is NOT a criticism of the functioning of the RTI regime?
o: Excessive speed in disposal of all RTI applications
nca6b0ff6c16.x: Appeal backlogs, vacancies, misuse of Section 8 and threats to activists are the identified concerns; excessive speed in disposal is not a criticism.

n5279b672cc0.s: Organisations excluded under Section 24 of the RTI Act must still disclose information relating to:
n5279b672cc0.x: Section 24 generally excludes listed intelligence and security organisations, but information on corruption and human-rights violations is not excluded.

n087f034070e.s: Who chairs the committee that recommends appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
n087f034070e.x: The committee is the Chief Minister (chair), the Leader of Opposition in the Assembly and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM; the Governor then appoints.

n069eaebd860.s: In June 2013, how many national political parties did the Central Information Commission declare public authorities under the RTI Act?
n069eaebd860.x: The CIC declared six national parties - INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP - public authorities; the Aam Aadmi Party was not among them.

nc06ac9f1411.s: Frivolous or bulk requests by applicants and bad-faith invoking of Section 8 by authorities illustrate that the RTI Act has been misused by:
nc06ac9f1411.x: Applicants misuse it through frivolous or bulk requests, and authorities through delays and bad-faith use of Section 8, so misuse is by both.

nc926ec83769.s: Max Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy is based on which type of authority?
nc926ec83769.x: Weber's ideal-type bureaucracy rests on legal-rational authority, with hierarchy, rules, impersonality, merit and written files, not personal patronage.

n2478f9bc182.s: The Fourth Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission was titled:
o: Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights
Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance
n2478f9bc182.x: The 4th Report was 'Ethics in Governance'; 'Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights' was the 10th Report.

nf26a9f4602a.s: Who is the custodian of Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building?
nf26a9f4602a.x: Mission Karmayogi (2020) runs on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and its custodian is the Capacity Building Commission, not the UPSC.

n3b82af81b76.s: Under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, on the ED's application the Special Court may confiscate a fugitive's property:
o: Only after a Supreme Court order
n3b82af81b76.x: On the ED's application, the Special Court may confiscate property even before conviction.

n0b1d32eab4f.s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, a knowingly false complaint is punishable with imprisonment up to:
n0b1d32eab4f.x: A knowingly false complaint attracts up to 2 years and ₹30,000; revealing a complainant's identity attracts up to 3 years and ₹50,000.

new.s: Which document of 1948 recognised the right to seek and receive information as a human right?
new.x: Article 19 of the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) recognised the right to seek and receive information.

new.s: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, whose jan sunwais started the RTI movement, was founded in Rajasthan by:
o: Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh
Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt
new.x: MKSS (1990) was founded by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh, not Medha Patkar.

new.s: Who was the first Chief Information Commissioner of India?
new.x: The CIC was constituted on 12 October 2005 with Wajahat Habibullah as the first Chief Information Commissioner. Vajja Srinivasa Rao is the AP State Chief IC.

new.s: The RTI Act came fully into force how many days after Presidential assent?
new.x: Assent was given on 15 June 2005 and the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005, after 120 days.

new.s: Which Section of the RTI Act, 2005 gives it overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923?
new.x: Section 22 makes the RTI Act override the Official Secrets Act, 1923.

new.s: Which Section of the RTI Act deals with complaints to the Information Commission and inquiry into them?
new.x: Section 18 covers complaints; Section 19 is appeals, Section 20 penalties and Section 25 the annual report.

new.s: Under which Section of the RTI Act can a request be rejected because it infringes the copyright of a person other than the State?
new.x: Section 9 allows rejection on grounds of copyright of a person other than the State; Section 11 deals with third-party information.

new.s: Under the RTI Act, information sought through an Assistant Public Information Officer must be supplied within:
new.x: An application through an APIO adds 5 days to the normal 30, making 35 days.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about time limits under the RTI Act:
1. Where third-party information is involved, the reply limit is 40 days.
2. The first appeal must be filed within 90 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct: third-party cases (Section 11) take 40 days. Statement 2 is wrong: the first appeal is within 30 days; 90 days is for the second appeal.

new.s: Under which provision of the RTI Act may exempt information be disclosed if public interest outweighs the harm, even if covered by the Official Secrets Act?
new.x: Section 8(2) is the public-interest override; 8(3) is the 20-year rule and 8(1)(j) covers personal information.

new.s: Cabinet papers are exempt from disclosure under which clause of Section 8(1) of the RTI Act?
new.x: Clause 8(1)(i) exempts cabinet papers; (d) is commercial confidence, (e) fiduciary relationship and (j) personal information.

new.s: Which agency was added to the Second Schedule of the RTI Act in 2011?
new.x: The CBI was added to the Second Schedule in 2011; the CIC is not exempt as it is the appellate body.

new.s: The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners of the Central Information Commission are appointed by the:
new.x: Under Section 12, the President appoints them on the recommendation of a committee of the PM, the LoP in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister.

new.s: Since the RTI Rules 2019, the term of an Information Commissioner is:
new.x: The original term of 5 years or 65 was replaced in 2019 by a term notified by the Centre, 3 years under the RTI Rules 2019.

new.s: What is the maximum penalty that an Information Commission can impose on a PIO under Section 20 of the RTI Act?
new.x: The penalty is ₹250 per day, subject to a maximum of ₹25,000.

new.s: Before the 2019 amendment, the salary of the Chief Information Commissioner was equal to that of the:
new.x: Originally the CIC's salary equalled the Chief Election Commissioner's and an IC's an Election Commissioner's; since 2019 the Centre fixes it.

new.s: Which provision of the RTI Act was rewritten into a blanket exemption for personal information by the DPDP Act, 2023?
new.x: Section 44(3) of the DPDP Act, 2023 rewrote Section 8(1)(j), dropping the public-interest override for personal information.

new.s: Which of the following was held by the CIC in May 2026 NOT to be a public authority under Section 2(h)(d) of the RTI Act?
o: Office of the Chief Justice of India
new.x: The BCCI is not substantially financed by government, so it is not a public authority; the CJI's office, financed NGOs and MPLADS works are covered.

new.s: The RTI (Amendment) Bill, 2013, which sought to exclude political parties from the RTI Act:
o: Was struck down by the Supreme Court
Was referred to the Law Commission
new.x: Parties did not comply with the CIC's 2013 order, and the 2013 Bill to exclude them lapsed; the matter is pending before the Supreme Court.

new.s: In Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v CIC (2012), service records, assets and tax returns of an employee were held to be:
o: Information that must be proactively disclosed
new.x: The Supreme Court held these to be personal information under Section 8(1)(j).

new.s: Which case held the office of the Chief Justice of India to be a public authority under the RTI Act?
o: Namit Sharma v Union of India
Zee Telefilms v Union of India
CPIO, Supreme Court v Subhash Chandra Agarwal
new.x: A Constitution Bench in CPIO, Supreme Court v Subhash Chandra Agarwal (2019) held the CJI's office to be a public authority.

new.s: The RTI Online portal for central public authorities, launched in 2013, is run by the:
new.x: The RTI Online portal (rtionline.gov.in) of the DoPT was launched in 2013 for applications, first appeals and online fees.

new.s: The 2026 inspection of 258 offices in 18 districts by the Andhra Pradesh SIC found violations of which provision of the RTI Act?
new.x: The AP SIC inspection found violations of Section 4(1)(b), the list of what must be proactively published.

new.s: In November 2023, the Andhra Pradesh High Court directed the State to set up:
new.x: Following the Supreme Court's Pravasi Legal Cell judgment, the AP High Court directed the state to set up an online RTI portal.

new.s: Which organisation released a 2025 report card finding significant gaps as the RTI Act turned 20?
new.x: The Satark Nagrik Sangathan 2025 report card found significant gaps in the functioning of the Act.

new.s: The Second ARC recommended linking the RTI regime with which law to protect RTI activists?
new.x: With over 100 RTI activists killed, the Second ARC urged linking RTI with whistle-blower protection; the 2014 Act is not operationalised.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides safeguards such as inquiry and hearing before dismissal of a civil servant?
new.x: Article 311 gives safeguards; Article 310 is the doctrine of pleasure and 312 the All India Services.

new.s: A member of a State Public Service Commission holds office for 6 years or until the age of:
new.x: SPSC/JSPSC members serve 6 years or until 62; UPSC members until 65.

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the functions of Public Service Commissions?
new.x: Article 320 lays down the functions of PSCs; 315 sets them up, 316 covers appointment and term, 317 removal.

new.s: The cadre-controlling authority for the IAS is the:
new.x: The IAS cadre is controlled by the DoPT, the IPS by the MHA and the Indian Forest Service by the MoEFCC.

new.s: Which ministry is the cadre-controlling authority for the Indian Forest Service?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
new.x: The MoEFCC controls the Indian Forest Service cadre.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four types of bureaucracy given by F. Morstein Marx?
new.x: Morstein Marx (The Administrative State) gave guardian, caste, patronage and merit bureaucracies; 'rational' is not one of them.

new.s: On 21 April 1947, Sardar Patel addressed the first probationers, calling them the 'steel frame of India', at:
new.x: Patel's address was at Metcalfe House, Delhi; the first Civil Services Day function was held at Vigyan Bhawan in 2006.

new.s: In which year was the first Civil Services Day function held at Vigyan Bhawan?
new.x: The first Civil Services Day function was held at Vigyan Bhawan on 21 April 2006.

new.s: Which committee (1976) recommended the three-stage Civil Services Examination of Prelims, Mains and Interview?
new.x: The D.S. Kothari Committee (1976) gave the three-stage CSE adopted from 1979.

new.s: Which committee (1989) recommended introducing an essay paper in the Civil Services Examination?
new.x: The Satish Chandra Committee (1989) recommended the essay paper and more weight to the interview.

new.s: The 12th Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission was titled:
o: Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance
Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights
Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance
new.x: The 12th Report was 'Citizen Centric Administration – The Heart of Governance'; the 4th was Ethics and the 10th Personnel Administration.

new.s: The first report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission (June 2006) dealt with:
new.x: The 1st Report was 'Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance' (9 June 2006).

new.s: How many reports did the Second Administrative Reforms Commission submit?
new.x: The Second ARC, constituted on 31 August 2005, submitted 15 reports between June 2006 and May 2009.

new.s: Political neutrality of central government employees is required by the CCS (Conduct) Rules of:
new.x: The CCS (Conduct) Rules 1964 and the AIS (Conduct) Rules 1968 require political neutrality and integrity.

new.s: In April 2026, an Andhra Pradesh section officer was dismissed for campaigning in the 2024 elections under:
new.x: The officer was dismissed under Rule 9 of the AP CCA Rules 1991 (G.O. Ms. No. 43).

new.s: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry into the civil services at which level?
new.x: The Second ARC recommended lateral entry at Joint Secretary level, along with performance-based appraisal.

new.s: Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, runs on which online platform?
new.x: Mission Karmayogi (2020) runs on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, with the Capacity Building Commission as custodian.

new.s: The Santhanam Committee led to the setting up of which two bodies?
new.x: The Santhanam Committee (1962-64) led to the CBI in 1963 and the CVC in 1964.

new.s: India signed the UN Convention against Corruption in:
new.x: UNCAC was adopted in 2003, signed by India in 2005 and ratified in 2011.

new.s: Under the 2018 amendment to the Prevention of Corruption Act, a coerced bribe-giver is protected if he reports the matter within:
new.x: A coerced bribe-giver is protected if he reports within 7 days, not 30.

new.s: The Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018 requires trial of corruption cases to be completed within 2 years, extendable to a maximum of:
new.x: The trial must finish within 2 years, extendable to a maximum of 4 years.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018:
1. Bribe-giving was made a direct offence punishable with up to 7 years.
2. Commercial organisations are liable for bribes offered on their behalf.
3. Its purpose was to align the law with UNCAC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: bribe-giving became a direct offence (up to 7 years), commercial organisations became liable, and the aim was alignment with UNCAC.

new.s: Which provision of the BNSS replaced Section 197 CrPC on sanction for prosecution of public servants?
new.x: Section 218 of the BNSS (in force from 1 July 2024) replaced Section 197 of the CrPC.

new.s: Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires government approval before:
o: Inquiry or investigation into official decisions
Arrest of a retired public servant
new.x: Section 17A requires approval before inquiry or investigation; Section 19 requires sanction before a court takes cognizance.

new.s: A complaint under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 must be made within:
new.x: Complaints must be made within 7 years, and anonymous complaints are not entertained.

new.s: Under the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, the competent authority for a complaint against a Union Minister is the:
new.x: Complaints against a Union Minister go to the Prime Minister; against a State Minister to the Chief Minister.

new.s: The Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015 was passed by the Lok Sabha in:
new.x: It was passed by the Lok Sabha in May 2015 and lapsed in 2019 with the 16th Lok Sabha.

new.s: Under which Act is the Central Vigilance Commission a statutory body?
new.x: The CVC is an independent statutory body under the CVC Act 2003; the DSPE Act 1946 is the basis of the CBI.

new.s: The Enforcement Directorate functions under which ministry?
new.x: The ED works under the Ministry of Finance, the CBI under the Ministry of Personnel.

new.s: Who was the first Lokpal of India?
new.x: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became the first Lokpal in March 2019; Justice A.M. Khanwilkar became chairperson in February 2024.

new.s: Besides the Chairperson, the Lokpal under the 2013 Act may have up to how many members?
new.x: The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to 8 members, 50% of them judicial.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Lokpal selection committee?
new.x: The committee is the PM (chair), Speaker, LoP, CJI or a nominated SC judge and an eminent jurist; the Cabinet Secretary is not on it.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's Lokayukta is established under the AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act of:
new.x: The AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act dates from 1983; the Lokayukta deals with higher functionaries.

new.s: Under the 2024 amendment, the AP Lokayukta is appointed on the recommendation of a selection committee chaired by the:
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
new.x: Since the 2024 amendment, a retired HC Chief Justice or Judge is appointed on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the CM, for 5 years.

new.s: Under the Benami Transactions (Amendment) Act, 2016, benami holding is punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to:
new.x: The Benami Act provides confiscation and up to 7 years' rigorous imprisonment, not ten.

new.s: Under the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018, the offence involved must be worth at least:
new.x: The FEOA applies where there is a warrant, an offence of ₹100 crore or more, and flight from India.

new.s: In the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025, India ranked:
new.x: In CPI 2025 India ranked 91st of 182 with a score of 39; in 2024 it was 96th with 38.

new.s: The Corruption Perceptions Index measures:
new.x: Transparency International's CPI, published yearly since 1995, measures perceived public-sector corruption from expert and business surveys.

new.s: Social audit of scheme works such as MGNREGA is carried out by the:
new.x: Social audit is the Gram Sabha's audit of scheme works under MGNREGA.

new.s: Citizen Report Cards of the Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru are associated with:
new.x: Citizen Report Cards were pioneered by Samuel Paul of the Public Affairs Centre, Bengaluru in the 1990s.
